summary: Gradual reserved-pool throughput evaporation during dense short-stream fanout — connector saturation and allocator heartbeat suppression
description:
Issue summary:
AtlasDocs reported a gradual but persistent drop in throughput for their dedicated reserved pool during repeated short-stream bursts (many concurrent 50–500ms streaming requests) beginning 2026-03-12 09:15 UTC. Total requests succeed but effective tokens/sec and slot utilization decline over a 6–20 minute window until either traffic subsides or a manual pool drain/reshuffle is performed.

Impact:
- Customer sees 30–70% reduction in delivered throughput on affected routes, p95 latency increases from ~180ms to ~700ms for batched endpoints.
- No 5xx errors observed; requests are delayed/queued at allocator attach and occasionally hit model-fallbacks.
- Affects AtlasDocs dedicated pool (reserved) and one other self_serve test tenant intermittently.

Environment:
- prod/us-east-1, dedicated cluster: pool-id rp-atlasdocs-03
- Serving runtime v2.9.1 with scheduler v1.4.0
- API gateway edge nodes us-east-1a/b/c

Steps to reproduce (customer):
1) Fire many short streaming generation requests (prompt size ~40 tokens, expected completion ~30 tokens) at high QPS (200–350 qps) from multiple client connections with keepalive off.
2) Observe sustained throughput degradation after 6–15 minutes: token/sec drops, slot attach latencies rise, allocator heartbeat count for pool controllers decreases.

Observed logs / metrics snippets:
- allocator.attach.latency.p50: increases from 120ms -> 420ms over 8 minutes
- pool.slot_utilization: 82% -> 34% over same window
- api.gateway.conn_state.syn_recv: spikes of ephemeral connections (thousands/min)
- sidecar.metrics: "heartbeat_missing_count": incrementing for pool controller pods
- no driver crashes, no OOMs, kernel logs clean

Initial hypothesis:
- Small, frequent streaming connections are creating ephemeral socket fanout at the API layer that pushes connector/backpressure into the scheduler/allocator, causing heartbeat suppression and delayed GPU attach.
- Connector (edge) connection churn causes sidecar to queue too many short-lived streams; this backpressures the allocator's health checks which then reduce preference for warm slots leading to cooler slot utilization and slower batch formation.

Customer-provided artifacts:
- Sample curl-based repro that mirrors their traffic generator (attached to ticket): atlas_repro_v2.tar.gz
- Grafana snapshots for rp-atlasdocs-03 (token/sec, attach latencies, connection churn)
steps_to_reproduce: Start a traffic generator that opens many independent HTTP/2 streaming sessions without connection reuse at 250 qps; each stream sends a short prompt and closes within 200-800ms.
Observe allocator.attach.latency and pool.slot_utilization in Grafana for rp-atlasdocs-03 over 10-20 minutes.
Run a controlled test with connection reuse (keepalive enabled, multiplexed streams) and compare slot utilization trajectory.

comments: 2026-03-12 10:02 - Support (Maya Chen): Acknowledged receipt. I've escalated to SRE/scheduler team and requested immediate telemetry dumps for pool rp-atlasdocs-03.

2026-03-12 11:14 - SRE (Diego Ramos): Early signal: api-gateway shows high SYN/connection churn; sidecar reporters show reduced heartbeat frequency for pool controller. Suspect connector saturation is starving the allocator's reconciliation loop.
2026-03-12 13:40 - Support (Maya Chen) -> Customer: Can you try enabling HTTP/2 connection reuse / keepalive on your generator for a 30-minute window? This has reduced reproduction in similar cases.

2026-03-12 14:05 - Customer (AtlasDocs, Rachel Lee): We enabled keepalive and observed throughput stabilized; tokens/sec returned to baseline in ~5 minutes. We'll keep running a longer test and report back.
investigation_notes: Checked scheduler logs between 09:10-09:40: several 'heartbeat_suppressed' marks when api-gateway reported >800 ephemeral_conn/sec.
Heap and CPU on pool controller pods normal; however the reconcile loop shows latency spikes when sidecar queue length > 1200.
Reproduced locally with small traffic generator: replication succeeds when connection reuse is disabled. Multiplexed streams did not reproduce the suppression.

Hypothesis refined: connector backlog (many short TCP streams) causes sidecar to prioritize connection processing; health pings for allocator are delayed, the scheduler marks nodes as less preferred and batch formation becomes sporadic leading to apparent throughput evaporation.
Related: small overlap with SUP-271998 (tenant-shadowing) but root cause here is connection-level fanout, not tenant CPU hogging.
short_term_workaround: Ask AtlasDocs to enable HTTP/2 keepalive / connection reuse (we provided code snippets).
Apply temporary edge-side rate limiting on ephemeral connections for rp-atlasdocs-03 to keep connector backlog < 500.
Manually trigger pool reshuffle / drain and warmup when sustained connector churn is detected (operator-runbook step).
long_term_action_items: (ENG) Implement backpressure propagation from edge connectors into allocator to avoid heartbeat suppression (ticket backlog assigned).
(SRE) Add a detector that alerts when ephemeral_conn_open rate > threshold and auto-apply soft connection-mitigation rules for dedicated pools.
(DEVX) Publish best-practice guidance for customers on streaming connection reuse and example SDK configs that lower connector churn.
(ENG) Evaluate improving sidecar accept loop scheduling to ensure allocator reconcile/pings maintain high priority.
Follow-up review with AtlasDocs after rollout of mitigations.
resolution: 2026-03-13 - Workaround accepted by customer: enabled connection reuse; throughput recovered in ~5 minutes during test window.
2026-03-14 - SRE applied a temporary soft-rate-limit at edge for pool rp-atlasdocs-03 during peak hours to prevent recurrence while long-term changes are scoped.
Pending: ENG work items to harden allocator resiliency and sidecar scheduling (linked PRs and tickets).
